scope: Drug information and pharmacovigilance practical sections for pharmacy students in Egypt: kept simple, 45 minutes per section.
criteria: Definitions (drug information, DIC, ADR, side effect, randomisation, hypothesis, power) match standard texts.
The systematic approach to a drug information query is complete and in the right order.
Tertiary, secondary and primary sources are classified correctly with real examples and their pros and cons.
Study designs and the evidence hierarchy are stated correctly and simply.
ADR classification (A-F) and causality methods (WHO-UMC, Naranjo) are correct, with scoring given accurately.
Each chapter can be taught in 45 minutes: no padding, tables over prose.
Added content (Sections 2 and 3) is marked and sourced.
MCQ distractors are plausible; rationales are one clear line.
exclusions: Advanced statistics beyond hypothesis, p-value, power and sample-size ideas.
evidence_expectations: Quote the exact text and give file and line for every finding.
Give replacement text, not only a critique.
Cite a standard textbook edition or a current guideline for any correction.
